blogs.title: When the Platelets Fall Too Soon: Early HIT After Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: This post would tackle one of the hardest bedside problems in cardiac surgery: separating expected cardiopulmonary bypass-related thrombocytopenia from pathologic platelet decline. Using this case, it would review why a progressive fall before POD5 should not dismiss HIT, especially when recent preoperative heparin exposure can trigger an early-onset or 'rapid' presentation.

blogs.title: Autoimmune HIT Is Not Just Severe HIT: Recognizing the Heparin-Independent Phenotype
blogs.description: This post would explain autoimmune HIT as a distinct clinical entity marked by heparin-independent platelet activation, profound thrombocytopenia, persistent hypercoagulability, and thrombosis despite stopping heparin. The case highlights practical clues that should push clinicians beyond 'routine HIT' thinking, including a platelet nadir of 13 x10^9/L, stroke, and delayed recovery.

blogs.title: Strong ELISA, Weird SRA: What to Do With Atypical HIT Laboratory Results
blogs.description: This post would focus on HIT diagnostics when the lab report does not fit textbook patterns. It would walk through the meaning of a strongly positive PF4 ELISA, serotonin release at 0 U/mL heparin, inhibition at high-dose heparin, and the unusual partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade—emphasizing how clinicians should integrate functional assays with pretest probability rather than overreact to the word 'indeterminate.'

blogs.title: Argatroban, IVIG, and Then Fondaparinux: Anticoagulating aHIT After Fresh Surgery and Stroke
blogs.description: This post would explore the management tension in severe postoperative HIT: the patient is profoundly prothrombotic, but also newly postoperative, thrombocytopenic, and has had an acute cerebral infarct. It would compare the rationale for initial argatroban, the role of high-dose IVIG in autoimmune HIT, and why persistent laboratory evidence of consumptive coagulopathy may justify switching to fondaparinux despite a therapeutic PTT on argatroban.

blogs.title: Falling Fibrinogen in a Thrombotic Disorder: HIT-Associated Consumptive Coagulopathy
blogs.description: This post would examine the underrecognized DIC-like end of HIT, where falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimer, and schistocytes signal uncontrolled thrombin generation rather than bleeding as the primary disease process. The case provides a platform to discuss how severe HIT can mimic TTP or sepsis-associated DIC and why serial coagulation markers can be useful adjuncts when monitoring treatment response.

blogs.title: Postoperative Delirium or Occult Stroke? Arterial Thrombosis in HIT
blogs.description: This post would use the patient's worsening delirium and ultimately discovered parietal infarct to highlight that HIT is not just a venous thromboembolism syndrome. It would discuss when subtle neurologic changes after cardiac surgery should prompt imaging, how HIT can present with arterial events, and why missing these complications can delay both diagnosis and escalation of anticoagulation.
